answer: On this Linux worktree a controlled stand-in shows stdio cost = 1.0 OS process per server per session (3 sessions x 2 servers = 6 processes) while one shared HTTP stand-in stays at 1 process with a LISTEN socket. The recorded driver 23 sessions x 65 servers = 2037 is arithmetically false (23*65=1495 by both Python and POSIX expr) and today's argv-exact MCP fleet count is 0, not 2037. Mechanism reproduced; fleet size and the 2037 figure are not.

claims.claim: One stdio stand-in MCP server costs one OS process per session; 3x2 produced 6 processes on /proc and on ps.
One shared HTTP stand-in costs one OS process for the same 3 sessions, distinguished by a LISTEN inode on /proc/<pid>/fd that stdio children lack.

The catalog's recorded equation 23 sessions x 65 servers = 2037 does not hold: both Python and POSIX expr compute 1495. Today's argv-exact MCP fleet on this box is 0, so the 2037 freeze size is not reproduced here.
claims.subject: recorded 23x65=2037 and today's live fleet size

completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0037 in the receipt AND a per-transport process count with a start/stop delta control and a stated proof the probe does not match itself

evidence.claim: Process count is an exact argv token, not a substring of the probe path; start/stop of one known server moves the count by +1 then back to baseline.
A second rail (/bin/ps plus per-pid fd/LISTEN handles) reproduces the same per-transport process counts.
23*65 is 1495, not 2037; live argv-exact MCP count is not 2037.

negative_controls.description: Substring 'RES-0037' matches this probe's script path and would report the measurer as a live server. The token matcher must stay silent on that PID.
A decoy argv includes probe1_self_exclusion_delta.py but not the stand-in token; the stdio token matcher must not count it.

notes: G-1 delivery of RES-0037. Live named probes measure stdio vs HTTP process cost with a start/stop delta and a stated self-exclusion proof. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. cloud ok is not consulted.
